title: Intrinsic comparison and cocycle for maximum histories
statement:
Let $V$ be totally ordered with least element $\bot$, and fix a resolution invariant calculus $\nu$ [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data]. Let $A=(X\hookrightarrow P)$ and $B=(Y\hookrightarrow Q)$ be embedded rational pairs [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution], and let $a:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism. Suppose $T_A,T_B$ are finite admissible maximum-extension histories [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history], each starting empty and stopping at its first regular strict transform, and label their extensions by their positive maxima in $L=(V\setminus\{\bot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$.

The isomorphism $a$ extends canonically to an intrinsic comparison of their labeled strict-transform histories. They have the same active labels and stop simultaneously. At every preceding label, the comparison identifies the two local invariant functions, their maximum values, and the reduced center ideals on the strict transforms. If $a_i:X_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_i$ is the comparison before a label and $I_i,J_i$ are the corresponding intrinsic center ideals, then $I_i=a_i^*J_i\,\mathcal O_{X_i}$, and the next comparison is the map of the intrinsic ordinary blowups in these ideals induced by $a_i$. It agrees with the strict transforms in the two ambient blowups and commutes with the transition maps. The comparison retains the ordered earlier ideals even when an intrinsic blowup is an identity. There is no assertion identifying $P_i$ with $Q_i$.

For $a=\operatorname{id}_X$ this gives the comparison for two embeddings of the same reduced scheme, with the identity comparison when the embeddings coincide. For three pairs and isomorphisms $X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}Z$, the comparison for $b\circ a$ equals the composite of the comparisons for $a$ and $b$ at every label. Thus three embeddings of the same scheme satisfy the cocycle law. The comparison also commutes with restriction and smooth ambient pullback whenever a diagram of initial pairs and isomorphisms is cartesian: after identifying the pulled-back histories and deleting empty centers, the pulled-back intrinsic comparison equals the comparison for the pulled-back initial isomorphism. The same assertions hold on all lower cuts of $L$, inserting identity stages at absent labels, and include length-zero and empty histories.

source.place: ILO Expose VIII 2.3.1, 2.3.4--2.3.5 and 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.91--94; conditional history argument extracted from lem-trf-embedded-resolution-ambient-comparison, old Steps 5 and 7: intrinsic blowup induction, transport by isomorphisms, and the cocycle. BMT Theorem 6.1 Addendum and section 6.3 are the underlying detailed reference, archival copy WANTED; no Stacks tag states this conditional resolution-history lemma.

proof.text: Write $H_i,K_i$ for the prefixes after $i$ extensions of the given histories, of lengths $r,s$. Every prefix is admissible: it is obtained from the empty history by its first $i$ maximum extensions. Inductively construct an intrinsic comparison of these prefixes over $a$, retaining all earlier center ideals in order. For $i=0$ the sole component is $a$, and there are no transition or ideal conditions. This is an intrinsic comparison of empty histories by [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. No identification of their ambient schemes is part of the induction.

Suppose the comparison through $i$ has been constructed, with final component $a_i:X_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_i$. Apply the intrinsic-value condition of [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data] to these two admissible prefixes. It gives $\nu_{H_i}(x)=\nu_{K_i}(a_i(x))$ for every $x$. Since $a_i$ is bijective on points, the two images in $V$ are equal. The regular-bottom condition implies that $X_i$ is regular exactly when $Y_i$ is regular: each is regular exactly when its invariant is bottom at every point. This includes empty schemes. If $i=r$ or $i=s$, first-regular stopping therefore forces both histories to stop here. Otherwise both have a next extension, their positive maxima are the same greatest element $m_i$, and the label of the next extension is the same element of $L$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; agent deduction from the stipulated calculus, not a new existence theorem

proof.text: At a nonterminal prefix let $I_i,J_i$ be the ideals on $X_i,Y_i$ of the next centers. Each center is the reduced full maximum locus, since these are maximum extensions. Thus they are reduced maximum-stratum ideals for the same $m_i$. The intrinsic-ideal condition of [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data], applied to the comparison already constructed, gives $I_i=a_i^*J_i\,\mathcal O_{X_i}$. These ideals are coherent, and in particular of finite type and quasi-coherent, by the maximum-geometry condition. Importantly, the condition is applied to prefixes already compared; no comparison of their next stages is assumed.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; intrinsic ideal clause of the conditional calculus

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] separately to $X_i\hookrightarrow P_i$ and $Y_i\hookrightarrow Q_i$, with their specified ambient center ideals. Their extensions to $X_i,Y_i$ are $I_i,J_i$, because the centers are specified closed subschemes of the strict transforms. The lemma identifies the given next strict transforms with $B_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(X_i)$ and $D_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}(Y_i)$, compatibly with their transition maps. These are the scheme-theoretic strict transforms, so no inference from topological containment is being made. The centers are coherent by Step 3, meeting also the finite-presentation convention in the definition of strict transform.

source.place: Tag 080E, lemma-strict-transform (1), with the morphism the closed immersion into the ambient scheme

proof.text: Let $p:B_i\to X_i$ and $q:D_i\to Y_i$ be their blowup maps. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $I_i\mathcal O_{B_i}$ and $J_i\mathcal O_{D_i}$ are invertible ideals. Step 3 gives $J_i\mathcal O_{B_i}=I_i\mathcal O_{B_i}$ along $a_i p$. Use [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] with its canonical quotient onto this extended ideal to obtain $f_i:B_i\to D_i$ with $qf_i=a_ip$. Apply it to $a_i^{-1}$ to obtain $g_i:D_i\to B_i$. Both $g_if_i$ and $1_{B_i}$ lie over $X_i$ and induce the same canonical quotient onto $I_i\mathcal O_{B_i}$, so uniqueness gives $g_if_i=1$; likewise $f_ig_i=1$. Conjugate $f_i$ by the identifications of Step 4 to define $a_{i+1}$. The equation $qf_i=a_ip$ supplies its transition square. Keep all previous components and ideal equalities; appending this one gives the next prefix comparison. An identity intrinsic blowup still contributes its recorded center and label.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 0806, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor and lemma-universal-property-blowing-up; universal-lift construction applied in both directions

proof.text: Finite induction using Steps 2--5 constructs all components and proves $r=s$: if one length were smaller, Step 2 at that terminal prefix would force the other to stop there as well. Every corresponding center and label agrees. The strict-progress clause of [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data] makes consecutive positive maxima strictly decrease in $V$, hence the active labels strictly increase in $L$ and never repeat. Thus the constructed prefix comparison is the required label-preserving natural isomorphism of the finite strict-transform histories [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. It identifies local values and center ideals at each prefix by Steps 2--3. This induction uses the finiteness in the hypothesis; it does not assume $V$ well-founded or invoke the existence of a resolution algorithm.

source.place: VIII 2.3.1 and 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.91,93--94; agent-written termination of the finite comparison induction

proof.text: For the identity initial isomorphism and the same history, its identity components are the constructed ones: inductively the next identity and the constructed map induce the same canonical quotient, so [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] identifies them. For two embeddings of the same $X$, use $a=1_X$ in Steps 1--6. For three histories write their components $a_i,b_i,c_i$, where $c$ starts at $ba$. At $i=0$, $c_0=b_0a_0$. If $c_i=b_ia_i$, both $c_{i+1}$ and $b_{i+1}a_{i+1}$ are maps from the same intrinsic blowup into the third intrinsic blowup over $b_ia_i$. Successive ideal extension sends its center ideal to the same extended ideal in the source, with the same canonical quotient: locally both operations send a section to its image and then multiply by source functions. Uniqueness gives equality at $i+1$. Induction proves the cocycle at every stage. Taking the three initial maps to be identities gives the change-of-embedding cocycle. This identifies the constructed comparisons; no assertion that every ideal-preserving diagram isomorphism is unique is needed.

source.place: Tag 0806, lemma-universal-property-blowing-up; agent-written identity and composition induction

proof.text: For the cartesian smooth ambient diagrams in the statement, [lem-trf-maximum-history-smooth-deletion] identifies each pulled-back history with its maximum history, retaining original labels and deleting exactly empty inverse-image centers. Its comparisons are cartesian on strict transforms and extend their center ideals. Let $a_i'$ be the pulled-back intrinsic isomorphism at a cut, with projections $u_i:X_i'\to X_i$ and $v_i:Y_i'\to Y_i$. Assuming the desired equality at this cut, the extended ideals satisfy $I_i'=I_i\mathcal O_{X_i'}=(a_i')^*J_i'\mathcal O_{X_i'}$: both sides are generated locally by the images of the same sections of $J_i$, since $v_i a_i'=a_i u_i$. Consequently emptiness of the two pulled-back centers agrees. At a retained label, the pulled-back next comparison and the comparison constructed for $a_i'$ both lie over $a_i'$ and induce the canonical quotient onto $I_i'\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i'}X_i'}$. By [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] they coincide. At a deleted label both transitions are the specified identities; omission leaves the equality intact. The initial equality is the assumed cartesian square, so induction proves compatibility at every retained label. Restriction is the open-immersion case of this same smooth pullback assertion.

source.place: Tags 0805 and 0806, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up and lemma-universal-property-blowing-up; ILO VIII 2.3.4--2.3.5 and 2.3.13, contracted smooth comparisons

proof.text: For a lower cut $D$ of $L$, let $k(D)$ be the number of common active labels in $D$. Assign to it the component $a_{k(D)}$ already constructed. If $D\subseteq E$, the transition is the composite of the intervening finite-stage transitions, so its naturality square follows by composing their commuting squares. If no active label lies between the cuts, $k(D)=k(E)$ and this square is the identity square. Identity, composition, and pullback equalities at cuts are therefore the equalities at these components, already proved. Unit-ideal identity stages at absent labels are the convention of [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]; they do not remove recorded earlier ideals. When the initial scheme is regular or empty, Step 2 applies at $i=0$, both lengths are zero, and every cut comparison is the given initial isomorphism. Thus all zero-length and empty-history cases are included.
